Apple is releasing the first Release Candidate (RC) version of macOS 26.6 to developers and public users, in preparation for the official system rollout. Below is the content of this update.

macOS 26.6 First Release Candidate Officially Launched

After five developer and public beta versions, Apple is now releasing the first Release Candidate of macOS 26.6, with the official update expected to arrive as early as next week.

Readers familiar with the beta testing cycle should know that macOS 26.6 does not include many new features, focusing primarily on bug fixes and performance improvements.

However, for users planning to upgrade to macOS 27 "Golden Gate" later this year, this update likely includes an important feature.

The release notes for the iOS 26.6 RC indicate that the system "optimises Spotlight indexing in preparation for iOS 27," so macOS 26.6 is expected to include the same changes. Once Apple publishes the macOS 26.6 RC release notes, this article will be updated immediately.

Another change specifically mentioned in the first beta was the fix for macOS deprecation notices appearing in some applications that were incorrectly identified as supporting only Intel processors. Subsequently, Apple also indicated it had resolved related issues with the ecosystem and HealthKit, but did not disclose other specific details about the update.

That said, we are reviewing this release and will report any noteworthy findings to our readers. The internal build number for the macOS 26.6 RC is 25G70.

How to Install the macOS 26.6 Release Candidate

Below is how to install the macOS Tahoe 26.6 Release Candidate:

  • Back up your Mac
  • Open System Settings
  • Go to General → Software Update
  • Click the "i" icon next to "Beta Updates"
  • From the drop-down menu in the top-right corner, select "macOS Developer Tahoe Beta"
  • Click "Done"
